91	def _set_expert_parameter_attributes(
92	    module: torch.nn.Module, parallel_mode: Optional[str], use_expert_pgs: bool
93	) -> None:
94	    """Set process-group and tensor-partition metadata on an expert TE module.
95	
96	    ``allreduce=False`` selects the expert topology, including EDP for gradient reduction.
97	
98	    Weights and biases, including TEGroupedLinear's numbered parameters, are also marked as
99	    TP-partitioned according to ``parallel_mode``; row-parallel biases remain replicated.
100	
101	    Any parameter which is partitioned along TP or ETP is marked with ``tensor_model_parallel``,
102	    which ensures that all shards contribute to the gradient norm.
103	
104	    Args:
105	        module: Transformer Engine module whose direct parameters should be marked.
106	        parallel_mode: Tensor-parallel mode used by the module (``"column"``, ``"row"``, or None).
107	        use_expert_pgs: Whether to use EP/ETP/EGTP/EDP process groups instead of TP/GTP/CP/DP.
108	    """
109	    for name, param in module.named_parameters(recurse=False):
110	        param.allreduce = not use_expert_pgs
111	
112	        name_match = _EXPERT_PARAMETER_NAME_PATTERN.fullmatch(name)
113	        parameter_kind = name_match.group(1) if name_match else None
114	        is_weight = parameter_kind == "weight"
115	        is_bias = parameter_kind == "bias"
116	        is_partitioned = parallel_mode in ("column", "row") and (
117	            is_weight or (parallel_mode == "column" and is_bias)
118	        )
119	        if is_weight or is_bias:
120	            param.tensor_model_parallel = is_partitioned
121	        if is_partitioned:
122	            param.partition_dim = 1 if parallel_mode == "row" else 0
123	            param.partition_stride = 1

421	def _gtp_pre_init(
422	    module,
423	    output_size,
424	    gtp_remat_group,
425	    extra_kwargs,
426	    *,
427	    is_expert=False,
428	    rng_via_kwarg=True,
429	    out_split_size=1,
430	):
431	    """Pre-shard ``out_features`` so plain TE builds this rank's shard; route init to a per-rank
432	    RNG region (``rng_via_kwarg=False`` for LayerNormLinear). Returns ``(out_features, gtp_ctx)``.
433	
434	    ``out_split_size`` is the factor TE further splits ``out_features`` by AFTER GTP (=tp_size for
435	    column-parallel, else 1). GTP pads the per-TP slice (``output_size // out_split_size``) so each
436	    rank's final shard stays alignment-divisible. Padding the full ``out_features`` would leave the
437	    post-TP-split shard mis-aligned (MXFP8 needs dims divisible by 32).
438	    """
439	    from megatron.core.tensor_parallel.gtp_api import gtp_remat_shard_dim0
440	    from megatron.core.tensor_parallel.random import get_gtp_remat_rng_tracker_name
441	
442	    assert (
443	        output_size % out_split_size == 0
444	    ), f"_gtp_pre_init: output_size={output_size} not divisible by out_split_size={out_split_size}"
445	    per_rank, pad_length = gtp_remat_shard_dim0(output_size // out_split_size, gtp_remat_group)
446	    shard_out = per_rank * out_split_size
447	    gtp_ctx = (gtp_remat_group, pad_length, output_size)
448	
449	    tracker_name = get_gtp_remat_rng_tracker_name(is_expert=is_expert)
450	    if rng_via_kwarg:
451	        extra_kwargs["rng_tracker_name"] = tracker_name
452	    else:
453	        module.rng_tracker_name = tracker_name
454	    return shard_out, gtp_ctx
455

457	def _gtp_attach_post_init(module, gtp_ctx, is_grouped=False):
458	    """Attach the GTP surface to a pre-sharded TE module's weights and restore logical out_features.
459	
460	    ``is_grouped=True`` for GroupedLinear (per-expert weight0..N, coalesced AG via weight_list).
461	    """
462	    from megatron.core.tensor_parallel.gtp_api import attach_gtp_to_presharded_module
463	
464	    gtp_remat_group, pad_length, logical_out_features = gtp_ctx
465	    # Restore the LOGICAL out_features (the sharded value was only needed to size the weight in
466	    # super().__init__): downstream code reads it, e.g. the grouped-MLP fusion gate checks
467	    # fc1.out_features == 2 * fc2.in_features (a shard-sized fc1 would silently disable fusion).
468	    module.out_features = logical_out_features
469	    attach_gtp_to_presharded_module(module, gtp_remat_group, pad_length, is_grouped=is_grouped)

472	@contextmanager
473	def _init_gtp_remat_context(
474	    module,
475	    output_size,
476	    gtp_remat_group,
477	    extra_kwargs,
478	    *,
479	    is_expert=False,
480	    is_grouped=False,
481	    rng_via_kwarg=True,
482	    out_split_size=1,
483	):
484	    """Wrap a plain TE constructor: yield out_features for ``super().__init__`` (pre-sharded under
485	    GTP), then attach GTP wiring on exit (skipped if construction raises, so it can't half-init).
486	
487	    ``out_split_size`` = tp_size TE splits ``out_features`` by after GTP (column-parallel), else 1.
488	    """
489	    if gtp_remat_group is None or gtp_remat_group.size() <= 1:
490	        yield output_size
491	        return
492	    out_features, gtp_ctx = _gtp_pre_init(
493	        module,
494	        output_size,
495	        gtp_remat_group,
496	        extra_kwargs,
497	        is_expert=is_expert,
498	        rng_via_kwarg=rng_via_kwarg,
499	        out_split_size=out_split_size,
500	    )
501	    yield out_features
502	    _gtp_attach_post_init(module, gtp_ctx, is_grouped=is_grouped)

505	def split_te_layernorm_column_parallel_linear(
506	    fused_layer,
507	    config,
508	    init_method: Optional[callable] = None,
509	    tp_group: Optional[torch.distributed.ProcessGroup] = None,
510	):
511	    """
512	    Split a TELayerNormColumnParallelLinear into separate TENorm and TEColumnParallelLinear layers.
513	
514	    Args:
515	        fused_layer: The fused TELayerNormColumnParallelLinear layer to split
516	        config: TransformerConfig to use for creating the new layers
517	        init_method: Initialization method for the linear layer (optional)
518	        tp_group: Tensor parallel group (optional)
519	
520	    Returns:
521	        A tuple of (TENorm, TEColumnParallelLinear) with weights copied from the fused layer
522	    """
523	
524	    # Extract dimensions from the fused layer
525	    in_features = fused_layer.in_features
526	    out_features = fused_layer.out_features * fused_layer.tp_size
527	
528	    # Create the norm layer
529	    norm_layer = TENorm(config=config, hidden_size=in_features, eps=fused_layer.eps)
530	
531	    with torch.no_grad():
532	        # Copy layer norm weight
533	        norm_layer.weight.copy_(fused_layer.layer_norm_weight)
534	
535	        # Copy layer norm bias if it exists
536	        if hasattr(norm_layer, 'bias') and hasattr(fused_layer, 'layer_norm_bias'):
537	            if fused_layer.layer_norm_bias is not None:
538	                norm_layer.bias.copy_(fused_layer.layer_norm_bias)
539	
540	    # Create the column parallel linear layer
541	    linear_layer = TEColumnParallelLinear(
542	        input_size=in_features,
543	        output_size=out_features,
544	        config=config,
545	        init_method=init_method or (lambda x: None),  # Dummy init since we'll copy weights
546	        gather_output=False,
547	        bias=fused_layer.use_bias,
548	        skip_bias_add=fused_layer.te_return_bias,
549	        is_expert=False,
550	        tp_comm_buffer_name=fused_layer.ub_name,
551	        tp_group=tp_group or fused_layer.tp_group,
552	    )
553	
554	    with torch.no_grad():
555	        # Copy weight
556	        linear_layer.weight.copy_(fused_layer.weight)
557	
558	        # Copy bias if it exists
559	        if fused_layer.use_bias and hasattr(fused_layer, 'bias'):
560	            linear_layer.bias.copy_(fused_layer.bias)
561	
562	    # TODO(Peter): Do we need this
563	    # Copy FP8 metadata if applicable
564	    if hasattr(fused_layer, 'fp8_meta') and fused_layer.fp8_meta is not None:
565	        if hasattr(linear_layer, 'fp8_meta'):
566	            # Copy FP8 scaling factors and other metadata
567	            for key in fused_layer.fp8_meta:
568	                if key in linear_layer.fp8_meta:
569	                    if isinstance(fused_layer.fp8_meta[key], dict):
570	                        for subkey in fused_layer.fp8_meta[key]:
571	                            if subkey in linear_layer.fp8_meta[key]:
572	                                linear_layer.fp8_meta[key][subkey] = fused_layer.fp8_meta[key][
573	                                    subkey
574	                                ]
575	                    else:
576	                        linear_layer.fp8_meta[key] = fused_layer.fp8_meta[key]
577	
578	    # Set the same configuration flags
579	    linear_layer.sequence_parallel = fused_layer.sequence_parallel
580	    linear_layer.is_first_microbatch = fused_layer.is_first_microbatch
581	    linear_layer.disable_parameter_transpose_cache = fused_layer.disable_parameter_transpose_cache
582	
583	    return norm_layer, linear_layer

626	    class TEFusedOpsMixin:
627	        """Shared lifecycle helpers for modules backed by TE fused ops.
628	
629	        Requirements and assumptions:
630	        - The mixin must appear before the concrete module class in the MRO.
631	        - Subclasses must call ``super().__init__`` so the mixin can initialize
632	          the unregistered fused-ops cache.
633	        - Subclasses must implement ``_make_fused_impl`` and return a
634	          ``te.pytorch.ops.Sequential`` whose parameters alias parameters owned
635	          by the registered MCore/TE modules.
636	        - The fused implementation is built lazily on first forward, after the
637	          concrete module has created its submodules and parameters.
638	        - The fused implementation must not be registered as a PyTorch
639	          submodule, because checkpointing and optimizer state should continue
640	          to use the original module hierarchy as the source of truth.
641	        - The fused implementation is an unregistered execution view over
642	          registered source modules and parameters.
643	        - Forward hooks on source modules are best-effort emulated on the fused
644	          implementation. Hooks that modify tensors are unsupported because TE
645	          fused ops do not expose intermediate tensors.
646	        - Hooks, config, and source module replacement after first forward are
647	          not reflected in the cached fused implementation. Call
648	          ``_reset_fused_impl`` before the next forward after such changes.
649	        """
650	
651	        _fused_impl: Optional[Tuple[te.pytorch.ops.Sequential]]
652	
653	        def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
654	            super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
655	            self._fused_impl = None
656	
657	        def _make_fused_impl(self) -> te.pytorch.ops.Sequential:
658	            """Construct the fused implementation."""
659	            raise NotImplementedError
660	
661	        def _get_fused_impl(self) -> te.pytorch.ops.Sequential:
662	            """Return the lazily-built fused implementation.
663	
664	            This owns cache initialization and hook registration for all fused
665	            wrappers. The fused implementation is stored in a tuple so PyTorch
666	            does not register the TE ops graph as a submodule with duplicate
667	            parameters.
668	            """
669	            if self._fused_impl is None:
670	                fused_impl = self._make_fused_impl()
671	                self._register_hooks_on_fused_impl(fused_impl)
672	                self._fused_impl = (fused_impl,)
673	            return self._fused_impl[0]
674	
675	        def _reset_fused_impl(self) -> None:
676	            """Discard the cached unregistered fused implementation.
677	
678	            This is intended for tests and for internal use after replacing
679	            source modules, changing config that affects TE ops, or changing
680	            hooks after the first forward.
681	            """
682	            self._fused_impl = None
683	
684	        def _register_hooks_on_fused_impl(self, fused_impl: torch.nn.Module) -> None:
685	            """Attempt to emulate submodule callback hooks.
686	
687	            This is not always possible because Transformer Engine's
688	            op fuser does not expose intermediate tensors. Depending
689	            on what kernel fusions the op fuser chooses, the
690	            intermediate tensors may not even exist. Hooks that modify
691	            tensors will result in incorrect behavior.
692	            """
693	
694	            # Get submodule hooks
695	            forward_pre_hooks = []
696	            forward_post_hooks = []
697	            backward_pre_hooks = []
698	            backward_post_hooks = []
699	            for submodule in self.modules():
700	                for hook_id, hook in submodule._forward_pre_hooks.items():
701	                    with_kwargs = hook_id in submodule._forward_pre_hooks_with_kwargs
702	                    forward_pre_hooks.append((submodule, hook, with_kwargs))
703	                for hook_id, hook in submodule._forward_hooks.items():
704	                    with_kwargs = hook_id in submodule._forward_hooks_with_kwargs
705	                    forward_post_hooks.append((submodule, hook, with_kwargs))
706	                for hook in submodule._backward_pre_hooks.values():
707	                    backward_pre_hooks.append((submodule, hook))
708	                for hook in submodule._backward_hooks.values():
709	                    backward_post_hooks.append((submodule, hook))
710	
711	            module_name = self.__class__.__name__
712	
713	            # Pre-forward hooks
714	            # Note: DDP pre-forward hooks are safe since they do not
715	            # interact with input tensor.
716	            if forward_pre_hooks:
717	                from megatron.core.distributed import distributed_data_parallel
718	
719	                if any(
720	                    inspect.getmodule(hook) != distributed_data_parallel
721	                    for _, hook, _ in forward_pre_hooks
722	                ):
723	                    warnings.warn(
724	                        f"{module_name} module has a submodule with a pre-forward hook. "
725	                        f"{module_name} module does not expose intermediate tensors, "
726	                        "so the hook may have incorrect behavior if it attempts to "
727	                        "access the input tensor."
728	                    )
729	
730	                def forward_pre_hook(module, *_) -> None:
731	                    for submodule, hook, with_kwargs in forward_pre_hooks:
732	                        if with_kwargs:
733	                            ret = hook(submodule, (), {})
734	                        else:
735	                            ret = hook(submodule, ())
736	                        if ret is not None:
737	                            raise RuntimeError(
738	                                f"{module_name} module does not expose intermediate tensors, "
739	                                "but submodule has pre-forward hook that modifies input tensor."
740	                            )
741	
742	                fused_impl.register_forward_pre_hook(forward_pre_hook)
743	
744	            # Post-forward hooks
745	            if forward_post_hooks:
746	                warnings.warn(
747	                    f"{module_name} module has a submodule with a post-forward hook. "
748	                    f"{module_name} module does not expose intermediate tensors, "
749	                    "so the hook may have incorrect behavior if it attempts to "
750	                    "access the input or output tensors."
751	                )
752	
753	                def forward_post_hook(module, *_) -> None:
754	                    for submodule, hook, with_kwargs in forward_post_hooks:
755	                        if with_kwargs:
756	                            ret = hook(submodule, (), {}, None)
757	                        else:
758	                            ret = hook(submodule, (), None)
759	                        if ret is not None:
760	                            raise RuntimeError(
761	                                f"{module_name} module does not expose intermediate tensors, "
762	                                "but submodule has post-forward hook that modifies output tensor."
763	                            )
764	
765	                fused_impl.register_forward_hook(forward_post_hook)
766	
767	            # Backward hooks
768	            if backward_pre_hooks:
769	                raise RuntimeError(
770	                    f"{module_name} module does not support submodules with pre-backward hooks"
771	                )
772	            if backward_post_hooks:
773	                raise RuntimeError(
774	                    f"{module_name} module does not support submodules with post-backward hooks"
775	                )

387	"""
388	The code below abstracts the functionalities needed for implementing "--fp8-param-gather" into
389	several functions. It provides different implementations for each function based on different
390	versions of TE, ensuring compatibility across various TE versions.
391	
392	Currently, there are three functions:
393	    - modify_underlying_storage
394	        This function is used in DDP to place all parameters into a contiguous buffer. For
395	        non-fp8 tensors, replacing their data is simple, just using code like
396	        "tensor.data = new_data". However, for fp8 tensors, their raw data is not stored in the
397	        ".data" attribute, and it varies with different TE versions and different recipes. This
398	        function provides a unified interface to replace the underlying storage of a fp8 tensor.
399	    - quantize_param_shard
400	        This function is used in dist-opt to cast fp32 main params to fp8 params. For non-fp8
401	        params, this casting is as simple as "bf16_params.copy_(fp32_main_params)"; but for fp8
402	        params, the casting logic varies with different TE versions and different recipes. This
403	        function provides a unified interface to cast fp32 main params to fp8 params, and also
404	        updates the necessary attributes (like amax, scale, scale_inv or transpose cache) of the
405	        fp8 model params.
406	    - correct_amax_history_if_needed
407	        This function is used to correct the amax history of fp8 tensors. In TE1.x, some inplace
408	        copy operations will write unwanted values to the amax_history of fp8 tensors. This function
409	        corrects the amax_history back. For TE2.x, it's an empty function.
410	        Only useful for delayed scaling.

418	    ) -> None:
419	        from transformer_engine.pytorch.tensor.utils import replace_raw_data

474	    def _quantize_param_shard_impl(
475	        model_params: List[QuantizedTensor],

480	    ) -> None:
481	        # Avoid circular import
482	        from megatron.core.optimizer.optimizer import _multi_tensor_copy_this_to_that
483	
484	        if len(model_params) == 0:
485	            return
486	
487	        if fsdp_shard_model_params is None:
488	            fsdp_shard_model_params = [None] * len(model_params)
489	
490	        for model_param, main_param, start_offset, fsdp_shard_model_param in zip(
491	            model_params, main_params, start_offsets, fsdp_shard_model_params
492	        ):
493	            if main_param is None:
494	                continue
495	
496	            if fsdp_shard_model_param is not None:
497	                shard_model_param = fsdp_shard_model_param
498	            else:
499	                shard_model_param = model_param._data.view(-1)[
500	                    start_offset : start_offset + main_param.numel()
501	                ]

503	            quantizer = model_param._quantizer
504	            # When not using --fp8-param-gather, the main_param (fp32) is first cast to bf16/fp16,
505	            # and then cast to fp8 during forward.
506	            # Although it's not necessary when --fp8-param-gather is enabled, we still keep this
507	            # logic to keep numerical consistency. So here cast the main_param to model_param.dtype.
508	            main_param = main_param.to(model_param.dtype)
509	            out = Float8Tensor(
510	                shape=main_param.size(),
511	                dtype=model_param.dtype,
512	                requires_grad=False,
513	                data=shard_model_param,
514	                fp8_scale_inv=model_param._scale_inv,
515	                fp8_dtype=model_param._fp8_dtype,
516	                quantizer=quantizer,
517	            )
518	            quantizer.update_quantized(main_param, out)
519	
520	        amaxes = []

520	        amaxes = []
521	        scales = []
522	        scale_invs = []
523	        for model_param in model_params:
524	            quantizer = model_param._quantizer
525	            amaxes.append(quantizer.amax.view(1))
526	            scales.append(quantizer.scale.view(1))
527	            scale_invs.append(model_param._scale_inv.view(1))
528	            model_param._reset_caches()
529	
530	        dummy_overflow_buf = torch.tensor([0], dtype=torch.int, device="cuda")
531	
532	        # Update scaling factors.
533	        packed_scales = torch.empty(len(scales), dtype=torch.float32, device=scales[0].device)
534	        packed_scale_views = [packed_scales[i].view(1) for i in range(len(scales))]
535	        _multi_tensor_copy_this_to_that(scales, packed_scale_views, dummy_overflow_buf)
536	        torch.reciprocal(packed_scales, out=packed_scales)
537	        _multi_tensor_copy_this_to_that(packed_scale_views, scale_invs, dummy_overflow_buf)
538	
539	        # Reduce amaxes.
540	        # Note: Assume each param has a separate amax.
541	        packed_amaxes = torch.empty(len(amaxes), dtype=torch.float32, device=amaxes[0].device)
542	        packed_amax_views = [packed_amaxes[i].view(1) for i in range(len(amaxes))]
543	        _multi_tensor_copy_this_to_that(amaxes, packed_amax_views, dummy_overflow_buf)
544	        torch.distributed.all_reduce(
545	            packed_amaxes, op=torch.distributed.ReduceOp.MAX, group=data_parallel_group
546	        )
547	        _multi_tensor_copy_this_to_that(packed_amax_views, amaxes, dummy_overflow_buf)

716	        config.num_layers_at_start_in_bf16 if config.first_last_layers_bf16 else 0

722	    # we are in the first or last pipeline-parallel rank are not needed.
723	    is_first_layer = layer_no < num_bf16_layers_at_start
724	    is_last_layer = layer_no >= config.num_layers - num_bf16_layers_at_end
725	
726	    if layer_no >= 0 and config.first_last_layers_bf16 and (is_first_layer or is_last_layer):

1	# Megatron Inference
2	
3	Use `MegatronLLM` (sync) or `MegatronAsyncLLM` (async, with HTTP serving via `serve()`) for typical inference workflows. Both classes hide the underlying engine pipeline (`DynamicInferenceContext` + `GPTInferenceWrapper` + `TextGenerationController` + `DynamicInferenceEngine`) and provide a vLLM-style `generate(prompts, sampling_params)` API. Choose **direct mode** (`use_coordinator=False`) when you manage data sharding yourself; **coordinator mode** (`use_coordinator=True`) when you want the engine to route requests across data-parallel replicas (required for HTTP serving).
4	
5	## Quickstart
6	
7	### Offline batch (sync)
8	
9	```python
10	from megatron.core.inference.apis import MegatronLLM, SamplingParams
11	
12	# Caller owns initialize_megatron(...), model construction, and model.eval().
13	# See examples/inference/offline_inference.py for a runnable end-to-end script.
14	with MegatronLLM(
15	    model=model,
16	    tokenizer=tokenizer,
17	    inference_config=inference_config,
18	    use_coordinator=False,
19	) as llm:
20	    results = llm.generate(
21	        ["Megatron inference is", "Hello, world"],
22	        SamplingParams(num_tokens_to_generate=64),
23	    )
24	    for r in results:
25	        print(r.generated_text)
26	```
27	
28	### OpenAI-compatible HTTP server
29	
30	```python
31	import asyncio
32	from megatron.core.inference.apis import MegatronAsyncLLM, ServeConfig
33	
34	async def main():
35	    async with MegatronAsyncLLM(
36	        model=model,
37	        tokenizer=tokenizer,
38	        inference_config=inference_config,
39	        use_coordinator=True,            # serve() requires coordinator mode
40	    ) as llm:
41	        await llm.serve(ServeConfig(host="0.0.0.0", port=5000))  # blocks until shutdown
42	
43	asyncio.run(main())
44	```
45	
46	## Public API
47	
48	| Symbol | Purpose |
49	|---|---|
50	| `MegatronLLM` | Sync entry. Methods: `generate`, `pause`/`unpause`/`suspend`/`resume`, `shutdown`/`wait_for_shutdown`. Properties: `engine`, `context`, `controller`, `is_primary_rank`. Context-manager protocol. |
51	| `MegatronAsyncLLM` | Async-flavored equivalent. Adds `serve(serve_config, blocking=True)` for HTTP. |
52	| `ServeConfig` | Dataclass for the HTTP frontend. Fields: `host` (`"0.0.0.0"`), `port` (`5000`), `parsers` (`[]`), `verbose` (`False`), `frontend_replicas` (`4`). |
53	| `SamplingParams`, `DynamicInferenceRequest`, `DynamicInferenceRequestRecord` | Re-exports from `megatron.core.inference`. |
54	
55	## Caller responsibilities
56	
57	- Call `initialize_megatron(...)` (full Megatron distributed setup) BEFORE construction.
58	- Call `model.eval()` BEFORE construction. The class does not toggle model state.
59	- Lifecycle methods (`pause`/`unpause`/`suspend`/`resume`) require `use_coordinator=True`; they raise `RuntimeError` in direct mode.
60	
61	## Future roadmap
62	
63	Planned new features:
64	
65	- **Dynamic streaming.** Offline streaming via `engine.async_step()`; HTTP streaming requires extending the coordinator / `InferenceClient` protocol to carry partial outputs (not just final request records).
66	
67	- **Weight update APIs.** `suspend_for_refit()`, `update_weights_from_collective()`, `resume_after_refit()` wrapping the existing resharding/refit primitives for RL workflows where weights swap between rollout steps.
68	
69	- **`megatron serve` CLI.** Single-binary launcher reusing `MegatronAsyncLLM.serve(...)`, with single-node and multi-node / headless modes — mirrors `vllm serve`.
70	
71	- **Config-based model construction.** `MegatronLLM(model="...")` style with model recipes and checkpoint resolution, removing manual model building from caller responsibilities.
72	
73	## Known limitations
74	
75	- **`MegatronAsyncLLM` requires `use_coordinator=True`** -- constructing with `use_coordinator=False` raises `ValueError` at `__init__`. The underlying `DynamicInferenceEngine` caches its loop reference at construction time and binds internal asyncio primitives (`_cond`, `_state_events`) to it. Coordinator mode rebinds those to a dedicated daemon-thread loop via `start_listening_to_data_parallel_coordinator`; direct mode has no such rebinding, so the synchronous `engine.generate()` path collides with the caller's running asyncio loop and raises `RuntimeError: This event loop is already running`. Use `MegatronLLM` for sync direct/coordinator workflows. Tracked for an upstream `engine.async_generate(...)` (or engine loop-rebinding) fix that would let `MegatronAsyncLLM` support direct mode.
76	
77	- **`llm.engine.reset()` is unsafe in coordinator mode.** Two failure modes, both upstream in `dynamic_engine.py`:
78	  - *Deadlock*: `reset()` *rebinds* (does not mutate in-place) `_cond` / `_state_events`. Any coroutine on the engine-loop task that is `await`ing one of those primitives holds a reference to the OLD object in its suspended frame. Subsequent `notify_all()` / `set()` calls hit the NEW objects, leaving the suspended waiter stranded; the next `generate()` hangs.
79	  - *Silent corruption*: `reset()` also sets `self.use_coordinator = False`, which silently re-routes failed-request handling, scheduling notification, and `suspend()`'s state machine to direct-mode branches. Outcome: not-a-hang but wrong behavior, harder to diagnose.
80	  - The example `offline_inference.py` blocks `--inference-repeat-n > 1` with `--use-coordinator` for these reasons. Direct-mode reset is safe.
81	
82	- **HTTP frontend is fixed to global rank 0.** There is no per-rank `role` override on `ServeConfig` to host the HTTP server on a non-rank-0 rank or to opt a rank out of HTTP. Control placement via the launcher (e.g., torchrun rank-0 placement), mirroring how vLLM's `--headless` is invoked today.
83	
84	- **Server returns `"model": "EMPTY"`.** The HTTP frontend doesn't expose a `ServeConfig.model_name` to echo in `/v1/completions` / `/v1/chat/completions` responses, doesn't validate the request `model` field against a configured name, and exposes no `GET /v1/models` discovery endpoint. Clients can still pass any `model` in their request body — the dynamic server ignores it.
85	
86	## Low-level APIs
87	
88	For step-level control, custom forward-step integration, or migration from existing pipelines, drop down to the building blocks in this directory: `DynamicInferenceEngine` (manual `add_request` / `step_modern` stepping), `DynamicInferenceContext`, `TextGenerationController`, and the model inference wrappers under `model_inference_wrappers/`. Runnable examples live in [`examples/inference/advanced/`](../../examples/inference/advanced/): `gpt_dynamic_inference.py` (manual stepping), `gpt_dynamic_inference_with_coordinator.py` (explicit coordinator + `InferenceClient` lifecycle), `gpt_static_inference.py` (static engine), and `simple_t5_batch_inference.py` (T5).
89	
90	## See also
91	
92	- Examples: [`examples/inference/offline_inference.py`](../../examples/inference/offline_inference.py) (4 modes via `--mode` / `--use-coordinator`), [`examples/inference/launch_inference_server.py`](../../examples/inference/launch_inference_server.py) (HTTP server).

1	# Repository Guidelines
2	
3	## Skills
4	
5	The `skills/` directory contains structured guides for common tasks (running
6	tests, building containers, managing dependencies, submitting SLURM jobs, etc.).
7	**Always read the relevant `SKILL.md` before starting any task it covers —
8	skills are mandatory context, not optional background reading.**
9	
10	**Workflow — mandatory order for every task:**
11	1. **Pull information first.** Read the commit, PR, error log, file, or
12	   whatever artifact the task is about. Do not reason about it yet.
13	2. **Select and invoke the skill.** Based on what you just read, identify
14	   the relevant skill and invoke it before forming any answer or plan.
15	3. **Answer or implement.** Only after the skill is loaded, use its context
16	   to reason, diagnose, or write code.
17	
18	Never skip or reorder these steps. Do not wait for the user to name the right
19	skill keyword — infer it from the artifact you read.
20	
21	## Contributing
22	
23	### Pull Requests
24	
25	- All PRs must be created as **drafts**. Use `gh pr create --draft` or the GitHub UI draft option.
26	- Never push branches directly to `https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM`. You must push your branch to a personal fork (e.g. `https://github.com/<your-username>/Megatron-LM`), then open a PR from the fork's branch against `NVIDIA/Megatron-LM`.
27	- Commit PR changes with both `-s` and `-S`: `-s` adds the required
28	  `Signed-off-by` trailer, and `-S` signs the commit so copy-pr-bot and `/ok to
29	test` can verify the pushed commit without manually specifying the SHA.
30	Megatron Core engineers at NVIDIA should sign using their NVIDIA emails so they
31	are automatically added to the right user groups on the internal Slack
32	workspace.
33	- Read @docs/developer/contribute.md for the full contribution policy, including code style, commit message conventions, and issue guidelines.
34	
35	### Code Quality
36	
37	- After editing imports in any Python files, always run `uv run isort` on those files to fix import order before committing.
38	
39	### Megatron Core Process Groups
40	
41	- In `megatron/core` production code, avoid adding new direct reads of global
42	  process groups from `parallel_state` (for example,
43	  `parallel_state.get_tensor_model_parallel_group()` or directly imported
44	  `get_*_group()` helpers). Prefer accepting a `ProcessGroupCollection` or an
45	  explicit `torch.distributed.ProcessGroup` from the caller and passing that
46	  through.

48	  `megatron/core/process_groups_config.py`, initialization/bootstrap code that
49	  materializes a `ProcessGroupCollection` from MPU globals, tests, docs, and

52	  `megatron/training` or other training-loop code unless the PR explicitly
53	  opts into that migration.
54	- In reviews, flag new direct `parallel_state.get_*_group()` usage in
55	  `megatron/core` unless it is one of the compatibility points above. This is
56	  advisory guidance, not a CI gate.

91	def _set_expert_parameter_attributes(
92	    module: torch.nn.Module, parallel_mode: Optional[str], use_expert_pgs: bool
93	) -> None:
94	    """Set process-group and tensor-partition metadata on an expert TE module.
95	
96	    ``allreduce=False`` selects the expert topology, including EDP for gradient reduction.
97	
98	    Weights and biases, including TEGroupedLinear's numbered parameters, are also marked as
99	    TP-partitioned according to ``parallel_mode``; row-parallel biases remain replicated.
100	
101	    Any parameter which is partitioned along TP or ETP is marked with ``tensor_model_parallel``,
102	    which ensures that all shards contribute to the gradient norm.
103	
104	    Args:
105	        module: Transformer Engine module whose direct parameters should be marked.
106	        parallel_mode: Tensor-parallel mode used by the module (``"column"``, ``"row"``, or None).
107	        use_expert_pgs: Whether to use EP/ETP/EGTP/EDP process groups instead of TP/GTP/CP/DP.
108	    """
109	    for name, param in module.named_parameters(recurse=False):
110	        param.allreduce = not use_expert_pgs
111	
112	        name_match = _EXPERT_PARAMETER_NAME_PATTERN.fullmatch(name)
113	        parameter_kind = name_match.group(1) if name_match else None
114	        is_weight = parameter_kind == "weight"
115	        is_bias = parameter_kind == "bias"
116	        is_partitioned = parallel_mode in ("column", "row") and (
117	            is_weight or (parallel_mode == "column" and is_bias)
118	        )
119	        if is_weight or is_bias:
120	            param.tensor_model_parallel = is_partitioned
121	        if is_partitioned:
122	            param.partition_dim = 1 if parallel_mode == "row" else 0
123	            param.partition_stride = 1

133	class TEQuantizationRecipe:
134	    """Class to capture options for opening an autocast context in forward"""
135	
136	    fp8_quantization_recipe: Optional[Fp8Recipe] = None
137	    """
138	    An FP8 quantization override if the module should use FP8.
139	    If no FP8 or FP4 quantization is configured, the recipe is execution
140	    in high-precision (BF16).
141	    """

143	    """
144	    An FP4 quantization override if the module should use FP4.
145	    If no FP8 or FP4 quantization is configured, the recipe is execution
146	    in high-precision (BF16).
147	    """
148	    custom_recipe_factory: Optional[str] = None
149	    """The path to a custom recipe factory if a custom Fp4 or Fp8 recipe is configured"""
150	    fp8_format: str = "e4m3"
151	    """A format to select from an FP8Recipe"""
152	    override_quantized_autocast: bool = True
153	    """
154	    If the quantization autocast context for a targeted module is enabled,
155	    whether to override it and change (or disable) the quantization recipe.
156	    """
157	    override_nonquantized_autocast: bool = False
158	    """
159	    If the quantization autocast context for a targeted module is not enabled,
160	    whether to override it and enable a quantization recipe.
161	    """
162	    tp_only_amax_red: bool = False
163	    """
164	    If an amax reduction is applicable, such as in per-tensor quantization recipe,
165	    whether to reduce only along TP groups.
166	    """
167	    fp8_param: bool = False

169	    If cast the initialized parameters to fp8 precision and all-gather weights in FP8.
170	    """

176	    @classmethod
177	    def parse_from_config(cls, quant_config: Dict[Any, Any]) -> "TEQuantizationRecipe":
178	        """
179	        Parse config from quantization dictionary.
180	        """
181	        kwargs = {}
182	        class_keys = cls.get_config_keys()
183	        for field in class_keys:
184	            if field in quant_config:
185	                kwargs[field] = quant_config[field]
186	        for field in quant_config:
187	            if field not in class_keys:
188	                raise ValueError(f"Field '{field}' not valid for this configuration.")
189	        instance = TEQuantizationRecipe(**kwargs)
190	        if instance.fp8_quantization_recipe == Fp8Recipe.delayed:
191	            raise ValueError("Delayed scaling not in scope of te per-module quantization config.")
192	        if (
193	            instance.fp8_quantization_recipe is not None
194	            and instance.fp4_quantization_recipe is not None
195	        ):
196	            raise ValueError("fp8 and fp4 quantization settings are mutually exclusive.")
197	        if (
198	            instance.fp8_quantization_recipe == Fp8Recipe.custom
199	            or instance.fp4_quantization_recipe == Fp4Recipe.custom
200	        ):
201	            if instance.custom_recipe_factory is None:
202	                raise ValueError("custom fp8 or fp4 recipe requires custom_recipe_factory")
203	        return instance

206	    def get_config_keys(cls) -> Set[str]:
207	        """Get expected keys from the dataclass fields."""
208	        return {field.name for field in dataclasses.fields(cls)}

421	def _gtp_pre_init(
422	    module,
423	    output_size,
424	    gtp_remat_group,
425	    extra_kwargs,
426	    *,
427	    is_expert=False,
428	    rng_via_kwarg=True,
429	    out_split_size=1,
430	):
431	    """Pre-shard ``out_features`` so plain TE builds this rank's shard; route init to a per-rank
432	    RNG region (``rng_via_kwarg=False`` for LayerNormLinear). Returns ``(out_features, gtp_ctx)``.
433	
434	    ``out_split_size`` is the factor TE further splits ``out_features`` by AFTER GTP (=tp_size for
435	    column-parallel, else 1). GTP pads the per-TP slice (``output_size // out_split_size``) so each
436	    rank's final shard stays alignment-divisible. Padding the full ``out_features`` would leave the
437	    post-TP-split shard mis-aligned (MXFP8 needs dims divisible by 32).
438	    """
439	    from megatron.core.tensor_parallel.gtp_api import gtp_remat_shard_dim0
440	    from megatron.core.tensor_parallel.random import get_gtp_remat_rng_tracker_name
441	
442	    assert (
443	        output_size % out_split_size == 0
444	    ), f"_gtp_pre_init: output_size={output_size} not divisible by out_split_size={out_split_size}"
445	    per_rank, pad_length = gtp_remat_shard_dim0(output_size // out_split_size, gtp_remat_group)
446	    shard_out = per_rank * out_split_size
447	    gtp_ctx = (gtp_remat_group, pad_length, output_size)
448	
449	    tracker_name = get_gtp_remat_rng_tracker_name(is_expert=is_expert)
450	    if rng_via_kwarg:
451	        extra_kwargs["rng_tracker_name"] = tracker_name
452	    else:
453	        module.rng_tracker_name = tracker_name
454	    return shard_out, gtp_ctx
455

457	def _gtp_attach_post_init(module, gtp_ctx, is_grouped=False):
458	    """Attach the GTP surface to a pre-sharded TE module's weights and restore logical out_features.
459	
460	    ``is_grouped=True`` for GroupedLinear (per-expert weight0..N, coalesced AG via weight_list).
461	    """
462	    from megatron.core.tensor_parallel.gtp_api import attach_gtp_to_presharded_module
463	
464	    gtp_remat_group, pad_length, logical_out_features = gtp_ctx
465	    # Restore the LOGICAL out_features (the sharded value was only needed to size the weight in
466	    # super().__init__): downstream code reads it, e.g. the grouped-MLP fusion gate checks
467	    # fc1.out_features == 2 * fc2.in_features (a shard-sized fc1 would silently disable fusion).
468	    module.out_features = logical_out_features
469	    attach_gtp_to_presharded_module(module, gtp_remat_group, pad_length, is_grouped=is_grouped)

472	@contextmanager
473	def _init_gtp_remat_context(
474	    module,
475	    output_size,
476	    gtp_remat_group,
477	    extra_kwargs,
478	    *,
479	    is_expert=False,
480	    is_grouped=False,
481	    rng_via_kwarg=True,
482	    out_split_size=1,
483	):
484	    """Wrap a plain TE constructor: yield out_features for ``super().__init__`` (pre-sharded under
485	    GTP), then attach GTP wiring on exit (skipped if construction raises, so it can't half-init).
486	
487	    ``out_split_size`` = tp_size TE splits ``out_features`` by after GTP (column-parallel), else 1.
488	    """
489	    if gtp_remat_group is None or gtp_remat_group.size() <= 1:
490	        yield output_size
491	        return
492	    out_features, gtp_ctx = _gtp_pre_init(
493	        module,
494	        output_size,
495	        gtp_remat_group,
496	        extra_kwargs,
497	        is_expert=is_expert,
498	        rng_via_kwarg=rng_via_kwarg,
499	        out_split_size=out_split_size,
500	    )
501	    yield out_features
502	    _gtp_attach_post_init(module, gtp_ctx, is_grouped=is_grouped)

505	def split_te_layernorm_column_parallel_linear(
506	    fused_layer,
507	    config,
508	    init_method: Optional[callable] = None,
509	    tp_group: Optional[torch.distributed.ProcessGroup] = None,
510	):
511	    """
512	    Split a TELayerNormColumnParallelLinear into separate TENorm and TEColumnParallelLinear layers.
513	
514	    Args:
515	        fused_layer: The fused TELayerNormColumnParallelLinear layer to split
516	        config: TransformerConfig to use for creating the new layers
517	        init_method: Initialization method for the linear layer (optional)
518	        tp_group: Tensor parallel group (optional)
519	
520	    Returns:
521	        A tuple of (TENorm, TEColumnParallelLinear) with weights copied from the fused layer
522	    """
523	
524	    # Extract dimensions from the fused layer
525	    in_features = fused_layer.in_features
526	    out_features = fused_layer.out_features * fused_layer.tp_size
527	
528	    # Create the norm layer
529	    norm_layer = TENorm(config=config, hidden_size=in_features, eps=fused_layer.eps)
530	
531	    with torch.no_grad():
532	        # Copy layer norm weight
533	        norm_layer.weight.copy_(fused_layer.layer_norm_weight)
534	
535	        # Copy layer norm bias if it exists
536	        if hasattr(norm_layer, 'bias') and hasattr(fused_layer, 'layer_norm_bias'):
537	            if fused_layer.layer_norm_bias is not None:
538	                norm_layer.bias.copy_(fused_layer.layer_norm_bias)
539	
540	    # Create the column parallel linear layer
541	    linear_layer = TEColumnParallelLinear(
542	        input_size=in_features,
543	        output_size=out_features,
544	        config=config,
545	        init_method=init_method or (lambda x: None),  # Dummy init since we'll copy weights
546	        gather_output=False,
547	        bias=fused_layer.use_bias,
548	        skip_bias_add=fused_layer.te_return_bias,
549	        is_expert=False,
550	        tp_comm_buffer_name=fused_layer.ub_name,
551	        tp_group=tp_group or fused_layer.tp_group,

626	    class TEFusedOpsMixin:
627	        """Shared lifecycle helpers for modules backed by TE fused ops.
628	
629	        Requirements and assumptions:
630	        - The mixin must appear before the concrete module class in the MRO.
631	        - Subclasses must call ``super().__init__`` so the mixin can initialize
632	          the unregistered fused-ops cache.
633	        - Subclasses must implement ``_make_fused_impl`` and return a
634	          ``te.pytorch.ops.Sequential`` whose parameters alias parameters owned
635	          by the registered MCore/TE modules.
636	        - The fused implementation is built lazily on first forward, after the
637	          concrete module has created its submodules and parameters.
638	        - The fused implementation must not be registered as a PyTorch
639	          submodule, because checkpointing and optimizer state should continue
640	          to use the original module hierarchy as the source of truth.
641	        - The fused implementation is an unregistered execution view over
642	          registered source modules and parameters.
643	        - Forward hooks on source modules are best-effort emulated on the fused
644	          implementation. Hooks that modify tensors are unsupported because TE
645	          fused ops do not expose intermediate tensors.
646	        - Hooks, config, and source module replacement after first forward are
647	          not reflected in the cached fused implementation. Call
648	          ``_reset_fused_impl`` before the next forward after such changes.
649	        """
650	
651	        _fused_impl: Optional[Tuple[te.pytorch.ops.Sequential]]
652	
653	        def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
654	            super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
655	            self._fused_impl = None
656	
657	        def _make_fused_impl(self) -> te.pytorch.ops.Sequential:
658	            """Construct the fused implementation."""
659	            raise NotImplementedError
660	
661	        def _get_fused_impl(self) -> te.pytorch.ops.Sequential:
662	            """Return the lazily-built fused implementation.
663	
664	            This owns cache initialization and hook registration for all fused
665	            wrappers. The fused implementation is stored in a tuple so PyTorch
666	            does not register the TE ops graph as a submodule with duplicate
667	            parameters.
668	            """
669	            if self._fused_impl is None:
670	                fused_impl = self._make_fused_impl()
671	                self._register_hooks_on_fused_impl(fused_impl)
672	                self._fused_impl = (fused_impl,)
673	            return self._fused_impl[0]
674	
675	        def _reset_fused_impl(self) -> None:
676	            """Discard the cached unregistered fused implementation.
677	
678	            This is intended for tests and for internal use after replacing
679	            source modules, changing config that affects TE ops, or changing
680	            hooks after the first forward.
681	            """
682	            self._fused_impl = None
683	
684	        def _register_hooks_on_fused_impl(self, fused_impl: torch.nn.Module) -> None:
685	            """Attempt to emulate submodule callback hooks.
686	
687	            This is not always possible because Transformer Engine's
688	            op fuser does not expose intermediate tensors. Depending
689	            on what kernel fusions the op fuser chooses, the
690	            intermediate tensors may not even exist. Hooks that modify
691	            tensors will result in incorrect behavior.
692	            """
693	
694	            # Get submodule hooks
695	            forward_pre_hooks = []
696	            forward_post_hooks = []
697	            backward_pre_hooks = []
698	            backward_post_hooks = []
699	            for submodule in self.modules():
700	                for hook_id, hook in submodule._forward_pre_hooks.items():
701	                    with_kwargs = hook_id in submodule._forward_pre_hooks_with_kwargs
702	                    forward_pre_hooks.append((submodule, hook, with_kwargs))
703	                for hook_id, hook in submodule._forward_hooks.items():
704	                    with_kwargs = hook_id in submodule._forward_hooks_with_kwargs
705	                    forward_post_hooks.append((submodule, hook, with_kwargs))
706	                for hook in submodule._backward_pre_hooks.values():
707	                    backward_pre_hooks.append((submodule, hook))
708	                for hook in submodule._backward_hooks.values():
709	                    backward_post_hooks.append((submodule, hook))
710	
711	            module_name = self.__class__.__name__
712	
713	            # Pre-forward hooks
714	            # Note: DDP pre-forward hooks are safe since they do not
715	            # interact with input tensor.
716	            if forward_pre_hooks:
717	                from megatron.core.distributed import distributed_data_parallel
718	
719	                if any(
720	                    inspect.getmodule(hook) != distributed_data_parallel
721	                    for _, hook, _ in forward_pre_hooks
722	                ):
723	                    warnings.warn(
724	                        f"{module_name} module has a submodule with a pre-forward hook. "
725	                        f"{module_name} module does not expose intermediate tensors, "
726	                        "so the hook may have incorrect behavior if it attempts to "
727	                        "access the input tensor."
728	                    )
729	
730	                def forward_pre_hook(module, *_) -> None:
731	                    for submodule, hook, with_kwargs in forward_pre_hooks:
732	                        if with_kwargs:
733	                            ret = hook(submodule, (), {})
734	                        else:
735	                            ret = hook(submodule, ())
736	                        if ret is not None:
737	                            raise RuntimeError(
738	                                f"{module_name} module does not expose intermediate tensors, "
739	                                "but submodule has pre-forward hook that modifies input tensor."
740	                            )
741	
742	                fused_impl.register_forward_pre_hook(forward_pre_hook)
743	
744	            # Post-forward hooks
745	            if forward_post_hooks:
746	                warnings.warn(
747	                    f"{module_name} module has a submodule with a post-forward hook. "
748	                    f"{module_name} module does not expose intermediate tensors, "
749	                    "so the hook may have incorrect behavior if it attempts to "
750	                    "access the input or output tensors."
751	                )
752	
753	                def forward_post_hook(module, *_) -> None:
754	                    for submodule, hook, with_kwargs in forward_post_hooks:
755	                        if with_kwargs:
756	                            ret = hook(submodule, (), {}, None)
757	                        else:
758	                            ret = hook(submodule, (), None)
759	                        if ret is not None:
760	                            raise RuntimeError(
761	                                f"{module_name} module does not expose intermediate tensors, "
762	                                "but submodule has post-forward hook that modifies output tensor."
763	                            )
764	
765	                fused_impl.register_forward_hook(forward_post_hook)
766	
767	            # Backward hooks
768	            if backward_pre_hooks:
769	                raise RuntimeError(
770	                    f"{module_name} module does not support submodules with pre-backward hooks"
771	                )
772	            if backward_post_hooks:
773	                raise RuntimeError(
774	                    f"{module_name} module does not support submodules with post-backward hooks"
775	                )

966	        implementation using TE's ops API that shares the base class parameters.
967	
968	        The fused implementation uses:
969	        - MakeExtraOutput: Forks the residual connection

981	            """

985	            # Op 1: MakeExtraOutput - forks the residual
986	            fused_impl.append(te.pytorch.ops.MakeExtraOutput())

989	            fused_impl.append(

2792	            local_expert_indices_offset = get_pg_rank(self._pg_collection.ep) * self.num_gemms
2793	            ep_axis = len(sharded_offsets)
2794	            extra_states = self._split_extra_state(full_state_dict["_extra_state"])
2795	            for gemm_idx in range(self.num_gemms):

2800	                }

2805	                    new_sharded_offsets = sharded_offsets
2806	                else:
2807	                    expert_prefix = prefix
2808	                    new_sharded_offsets = (
2809	                        *sharded_offsets,
2810	                        (ep_axis, global_expert_idx, num_global_experts),
2811	                    )

2813	                    state_dict,
2814	                    '',

177	    grouped_tensor = _unwrap_parameter_data(tensor)

193	def copy_tensor_to_quantized_param(param: torch.Tensor, src: torch.Tensor) -> None:
194	    """Copy high-precision values into TE quantized parameter storage."""
195	    dst = _unwrap_parameter_data(param)
196	
197	    if is_grouped_tensor_with_quantized_storage(dst):
198	        if src.numel() != dst.numel():
199	            raise ValueError(
200	                "Grouped quantized parameter copy size mismatch: "
201	                f"src numel={src.numel()}, dst numel={dst.numel()}"
202	            )
203	        if not dst.all_same_shape():
204	            raise NotImplementedError(
205	                "Copying into grouped quantized parameters requires uniform member shapes."
206	            )
207	
208	        # Grouped quantized tensors cannot use GroupedTensor.copy_ here because
209	        # the generic grouped path can rebuild member tensors through
210	        # split_into_quantized_tensors(), which is not graph safe. Update cached
211	        # member tensors in place instead.
212	        quantized_members = get_grouped_quantized_members(dst)
213	        src_members = src.view(dst.shape).unbind(dim=0)
214	        if len(src_members) != len(quantized_members):
215	            raise RuntimeError(
216	                "Grouped quantized parameter member count mismatch: "
217	                f"src members={len(src_members)}, dst members={len(quantized_members)}"
218	            )
219	
220	        for src_member, dst_member in zip(src_members, quantized_members):
221	            dst.quantizer.update_quantized(src_member, dst_member)
222	        return
223	
224	    # Plain TE quantized tensors override copy_ to requantize into their
225	    # backing storage.
226	    dst.copy_(src.view(dst.shape))

229	def copy_tensors_to_quantized_params(params: List[torch.Tensor], srcs: List[torch.Tensor]) -> None:
230	    """List form of :func:`copy_tensor_to_quantized_param`, for a whole bucket of params.
231	
232	    Same values, minus the per-param ``copy_`` and tensor-subclass dispatch: the quantizer is
233	    resolved up front and called directly. Cast kernels are unchanged, one per param. Worth it
234	    because those casts are small and issuing them is expensive, and under
235	    --reuse-grad-buf-for-mxfp8-param-ag they run inside the forward pass.
236	
237	    Args:
238	        params: quantized model params to write into.
239	        srcs: high-precision source values, one per param, in the same order.
240	    """
241	    if len(params) == 0:
242	        return
243	
244	    srcs_to_cast = []
245	    dsts_to_cast = []
246	    quantizers = []
247	    for param, src in zip(params, srcs):
248	        dst = _unwrap_parameter_data(param)
249	        quantizer = (
250	            None
251	            if is_grouped_tensor_with_quantized_storage(dst)
252	            else getattr(dst, "_quantizer", None)
253	        )
254	        if quantizer is None:
255	            # Grouped storage quantizes per member; a missing quantizer has to be built. Both
256	            # cases are handled by the single-param path.
257	            copy_tensor_to_quantized_param(param, src)
258	            continue
259	        srcs_to_cast.append(src.view(dst.shape))
260	        dsts_to_cast.append(dst)
261	        quantizers.append(quantizer)
262	
263	    # Equivalent to dst.copy_(src), but entered directly instead of via the aten::copy_ op,
264	    # QuantizedTensor.__torch_dispatch__ (type and usage checks) and dst.quantize_(src).
265	    for src, quantizer, dst in zip(srcs_to_cast, quantizers, dsts_to_cast):
266	        quantizer.update_quantized(src, dst)

269	def modify_grouped_tensor_rowwise_storage(tensor: torch.Tensor, new_storage: torch.Tensor) -> None:
270	    """Replace a high-precision Transformer Engine GroupedTensor's rowwise storage."""
271	    tensor = _unwrap_parameter_data(tensor)
272	    if not is_grouped_tensor(tensor):
273	        raise ValueError("modify_grouped_tensor_rowwise_storage expects a GroupedTensor.")
274	    if is_grouped_tensor_with_quantized_storage(tensor):
275	        raise ValueError(
276	            "modify_grouped_tensor_rowwise_storage only supports high-precision GroupedTensor "
277	            "storage. Quantized grouped storage also owns scale buffers."
278	        )
279	
280	    old_rowwise_data = getattr(tensor, "rowwise_data", None)
281	    if old_rowwise_data is None:
282	        raise RuntimeError("GroupedTensor is missing rowwise_data.")
283	
284	    new_storage = new_storage.view(-1)
285	    if old_rowwise_data.numel() != new_storage.numel():
286	        raise ValueError(
287	            "GroupedTensor backing storage size mismatch: "
288	            f"old numel={old_rowwise_data.numel()}, new numel={new_storage.numel()}"
289	        )
290	    if old_rowwise_data.dtype != new_storage.dtype:
291	        raise ValueError(
292	            "GroupedTensor backing storage dtype mismatch: "
293	            f"old dtype={old_rowwise_data.dtype}, new dtype={new_storage.dtype}"
294	        )
295	
296	    new_storage.detach().copy_(old_rowwise_data)
297	    tensor.rowwise_data = new_storage
298	    tensor.columnwise_data = None
299	    tensor.quantized_tensors = None
300	    del old_rowwise_data

311	def _resolve_callable_from_python_import_path(dotted_path: str):
312	    """Resolve a Python import path like 'pkg.mod.func' to a callable.
313	
314	    Raises ValueError with clear message on failure.
315	    """
316	    if not isinstance(dotted_path, str) or not dotted_path:
317	        raise ValueError(
318	            "fp8_quantizer_factory must be a non-empty string with format 'pkg.mod.func'."
319	        )
320	
321	    parts = dotted_path.rsplit(".", 1)
322	    if len(parts) == 1:
323	        raise ValueError(f"Invalid fp8_quantizer_factory '{dotted_path}'. Expected 'pkg.mod.func'.")
324	    module_path, attr = parts[0], parts[1]
325	
326	    try:
327	        mod = importlib.import_module(module_path)
328	    except Exception as exc:
329	        raise ValueError(
330	            f"Failed to import module '{module_path}' for fp8_quantizer_factory: {exc}"
331	        ) from exc
332	
333	    fn = getattr(mod, attr, None)
334	    if fn is None:
335	        raise ValueError(
336	            f"Attribute '{attr}' not found in module '{module_path}' for fp8_quantizer_factory."
337	        )
338	    if not callable(fn):
339	        raise ValueError(
340	            f"Resolved attribute '{module_path}.{attr}' is not callable for fp8_quantizer_factory."
341	        )
342	    return fn

387	"""
388	The code below abstracts the functionalities needed for implementing "--fp8-param-gather" into
389	several functions. It provides different implementations for each function based on different
390	versions of TE, ensuring compatibility across various TE versions.
391	
392	Currently, there are three functions:
393	    - modify_underlying_storage
394	        This function is used in DDP to place all parameters into a contiguous buffer. For
395	        non-fp8 tensors, replacing their data is simple, just using code like
396	        "tensor.data = new_data". However, for fp8 tensors, their raw data is not stored in the
397	        ".data" attribute, and it varies with different TE versions and different recipes. This
398	        function provides a unified interface to replace the underlying storage of a fp8 tensor.
399	    - quantize_param_shard
400	        This function is used in dist-opt to cast fp32 main params to fp8 params. For non-fp8
401	        params, this casting is as simple as "bf16_params.copy_(fp32_main_params)"; but for fp8
402	        params, the casting logic varies with different TE versions and different recipes. This
403	        function provides a unified interface to cast fp32 main params to fp8 params, and also
404	        updates the necessary attributes (like amax, scale, scale_inv or transpose cache) of the
405	        fp8 model params.
406	    - correct_amax_history_if_needed
407	        This function is used to correct the amax history of fp8 tensors. In TE1.x, some inplace
408	        copy operations will write unwanted values to the amax_history of fp8 tensors. This function
409	        corrects the amax_history back. For TE2.x, it's an empty function.
410	        Only useful for delayed scaling.
411	"""
412	if HAVE_TE and is_te_min_version("2.2"):
413	    # Supported TE versions: 2.2+
414	    from transformer_engine.pytorch.tensor import QuantizedTensor
415	
416	    def _modify_underlying_storage_impl(
417	        fp8_tensor: QuantizedTensor, new_raw_data: torch.Tensor
418	    ) -> None:
419	        from transformer_engine.pytorch.tensor.utils import replace_raw_data
420	
421	        replace_raw_data(fp8_tensor, new_raw_data)
422	
423	    def _quantize_param_shard_impl(
424	        model_params: List[QuantizedTensor],
425	        main_params: List[torch.Tensor],
426	        start_offsets: List[int],
427	        data_parallel_group: torch.distributed.ProcessGroup,
428	        fsdp_shard_model_params: Optional[List[torch.Tensor]] = None,
429	    ) -> None:
430	        if len(model_params) == 0:
431	            return
432	
433	        from transformer_engine.pytorch.tensor.utils import cast_master_weights_to_fp8
434	
435	        args = [model_params, main_params, start_offsets, data_parallel_group]
436	        if fsdp_shard_model_params is not None:
437	            if not HAVE_PACKAGING:
438	                raise ImportError(
439	                    "packaging not found, please install it with `pip install packaging`"
440	                )
441	            if get_te_version() == PkgVersion("2.3.0.dev0+5fdd7bb") or is_te_min_version("2.3.0"):
442	                args.append(fsdp_shard_model_params)
443	            else:
444	                raise NotImplementedError(
445	                    f"FSDP with --fp8-param-gather is not supported in TE v{get_te_version()}"
446	                )
447	
448	        # For newer TE versions (i.e., have post_all_gather_processing function), we keep the
449	        # columnwise data and manually call post_all_gather_processing after all-gather, this
450	        # makes fp8 params compatible with CUDA graph.
451	        kwargs = {}
452	        if te_post_all_gather_processing is not None:
453	            kwargs["manual_post_all_gather_processing"] = True
454	
455	        cast_master_weights_to_fp8(*args, **kwargs)

457	    def _correct_amax_history_if_needed_impl(model: List[torch.nn.Module]) -> None:
458	        pass

460	elif HAVE_TE and is_te_min_version("2.0"):

462	    from transformer_engine.pytorch.tensor import QuantizedTensor
463	    from transformer_engine.pytorch.tensor.float8_tensor import Float8Tensor

465	    def _modify_underlying_storage_impl(
466	        fp8_tensor: QuantizedTensor, new_raw_data: torch.Tensor
467	    ) -> None:
468	        old_raw_data = fp8_tensor._data
469	        assert old_raw_data.dtype == new_raw_data.dtype
470	        new_raw_data.detach().copy_(old_raw_data)
471	        fp8_tensor._data = new_raw_data
472	        del old_raw_data

474	    def _quantize_param_shard_impl(
475	        model_params: List[QuantizedTensor],
476	        main_params: List[torch.Tensor],
477	        start_offsets: List[int],
478	        data_parallel_group: torch.distributed.ProcessGroup,
479	        fsdp_shard_model_params: Optional[List[torch.Tensor]] = None,
480	    ) -> None:
481	        # Avoid circular import
482	        from megatron.core.optimizer.optimizer import _multi_tensor_copy_this_to_that
483	
484	        if len(model_params) == 0:
485	            return
486	
487	        if fsdp_shard_model_params is None:
488	            fsdp_shard_model_params = [None] * len(model_params)
489	
490	        for model_param, main_param, start_offset, fsdp_shard_model_param in zip(
491	            model_params, main_params, start_offsets, fsdp_shard_model_params
492	        ):
493	            if main_param is None:
494	                continue
495	
496	            if fsdp_shard_model_param is not None:
497	                shard_model_param = fsdp_shard_model_param
498	            else:
499	                shard_model_param = model_param._data.view(-1)[
500	                    start_offset : start_offset + main_param.numel()
501	                ]
502	
503	            quantizer = model_param._quantizer
504	            # When not using --fp8-param-gather, the main_param (fp32) is first cast to bf16/fp16,
505	            # and then cast to fp8 during forward.
506	            # Although it's not necessary when --fp8-param-gather is enabled, we still keep this
507	            # logic to keep numerical consistency. So here cast the main_param to model_param.dtype.
508	            main_param = main_param.to(model_param.dtype)
509	            out = Float8Tensor(
510	                shape=main_param.size(),
511	                dtype=model_param.dtype,
512	                requires_grad=False,
513	                data=shard_model_param,
514	                fp8_scale_inv=model_param._scale_inv,
515	                fp8_dtype=model_param._fp8_dtype,
516	                quantizer=quantizer,
517	            )
518	            quantizer.update_quantized(main_param, out)
519	
520	        amaxes = []

520	        amaxes = []
521	        scales = []
522	        scale_invs = []
523	        for model_param in model_params:
524	            quantizer = model_param._quantizer
525	            amaxes.append(quantizer.amax.view(1))
526	            scales.append(quantizer.scale.view(1))
527	            scale_invs.append(model_param._scale_inv.view(1))
528	            model_param._reset_caches()
529	
530	        dummy_overflow_buf = torch.tensor([0], dtype=torch.int, device="cuda")
531	
532	        # Update scaling factors.
533	        packed_scales = torch.empty(len(scales), dtype=torch.float32, device=scales[0].device)
534	        packed_scale_views = [packed_scales[i].view(1) for i in range(len(scales))]
535	        _multi_tensor_copy_this_to_that(scales, packed_scale_views, dummy_overflow_buf)
536	        torch.reciprocal(packed_scales, out=packed_scales)
537	        _multi_tensor_copy_this_to_that(packed_scale_views, scale_invs, dummy_overflow_buf)
538	
539	        # Reduce amaxes.
540	        # Note: Assume each param has a separate amax.
541	        packed_amaxes = torch.empty(len(amaxes), dtype=torch.float32, device=amaxes[0].device)
542	        packed_amax_views = [packed_amaxes[i].view(1) for i in range(len(amaxes))]
543	        _multi_tensor_copy_this_to_that(amaxes, packed_amax_views, dummy_overflow_buf)
544	        torch.distributed.all_reduce(
545	            packed_amaxes, op=torch.distributed.ReduceOp.MAX, group=data_parallel_group
546	        )
547	        _multi_tensor_copy_this_to_that(packed_amax_views, amaxes, dummy_overflow_buf)
548

550	        pass

918	    def _wrap_te_linear_for_padding(module: torch.nn.Module):
919	        """Wrap a TE linear module to automatically pad sequences for FP8 inference.
920	
921	        Modifies the module's forward method to:
922	        1. Pad input sequences to FP8 alignment requirements
923	        2. Run the original forward pass
924	        3. Unpad outputs to original sequence length
925	
926	        Args:
927	            module: A Transformer Engine linear layer (TELinear, TEColumnParallelLinear, etc.)
928	        """
929	        if module in _fp8_inference_wrapped_modules:
930	            return
931	        _pad_func = Fp8Padding(1)
932	        _unpad_func = Fp8Unpadding(1)
933	
934	        original_forward = module.forward
935	
936	        @wraps(original_forward)
937	        def padded_forward(input_tensor, *args, **kwargs):
938	            is_context_quantized = FP8GlobalStateManager.is_fp8_enabled()
939	            if hasattr(module, "will_execute_quantized"):
940	                module_uses_quant = module.will_execute_quantized(is_context_quantized)
941	            else:
942	                module_uses_quant = is_context_quantized
943	            # Only do padding for fp8 if we are in fp8 or fp4 context
944	            if not module_uses_quant:
945	                return original_forward(input_tensor, *args, **kwargs)
946	
947	            # With sequence parallelism we need to all-gather before padding
948	            # and reduce-scatter after unpadding
949	            if is_sequence_parallel := getattr(module, "sequence_parallel", False):
950	                if is_column_parallel_linear(module):
951	                    input_tensor = gather_from_sequence_parallel_region(
952	                        input_tensor, group=module.tp_group
953	                    )
954	
955	                # Disable sequence parallelism on the module because we are handling the
956	                # all-gather and reduce-scatter externally
957	                module.sequence_parallel = False
958	
959	            seq_len, batch_size, hidden_size = input_tensor.shape
960	            # Reshape to (S, B*H) to pad sequence dimension
961	            input_2d = input_tensor.reshape(seq_len, -1)
962	            # Pad the sequence dimension
963	            padded_input_2d, _ = _pad_func(input_2d, [seq_len])
964	            padded_seq_len = padded_input_2d.shape[0]
965	
966	            # Reshape back to (padded_S, B, H)
967	            padded_input_3d = padded_input_2d.view(padded_seq_len, batch_size, hidden_size)
968	            output = original_forward(padded_input_3d, *args, **kwargs)
969	
970	            # Handle output
971	            if isinstance(output, tuple):
972	                output_tensor = output[0]
973	                other_outputs = output[1:]
974	            else:
975	                output_tensor = output
976	                other_outputs = ()
977	
978	            # Unpad output - reshape to 2D, unpad, reshape back
979	            _, _, output_hidden_size = output_tensor.shape
980	            output_2d = output_tensor.reshape(padded_seq_len, -1)
981	            unpadded_output_2d = _unpad_func(output_2d, [seq_len])
982	            unpadded_output = unpadded_output_2d.reshape(seq_len, batch_size, output_hidden_size)
983	
984	            if is_sequence_parallel:
985	                # Reduce-scatter after unpadding
986	                if is_row_parallel_linear(module):
987	                    unpadded_output = reduce_scatter_to_sequence_parallel_region(
988	                        unpadded_output, group=module.tp_group
989	                    )
990	
991	                # Reset sequence parallelism flag on the module
992	                module.sequence_parallel = True
993	
994	            if other_outputs:
995	                return (unpadded_output,) + other_outputs
996	            else:
997	                return unpadded_output
998	
999	        module.forward = padded_forward
1000	        _fp8_inference_wrapped_modules.add(module)

80	def modify_nvfp4_rowwise_storage(fp4_tensor: torch.Tensor, new_rowwise_data: torch.Tensor) -> None:
81	    """Replace NVFP4 tensor's rowwise raw data with a new uint8 storage view.
82	
83	    Copies existing bytes into the new buffer, then swaps the underlying pointer.
84	    """
85	    if not is_nvfp4tensor(fp4_tensor):
86	        raise ValueError("modify_nvfp4_rowwise_storage expects an NVFP4 tensor")
87	    # Access TE's internal storage fields
88	    old_rowwise = getattr(fp4_tensor, "_rowwise_data", None)
89	    if old_rowwise is None:
90	        raise RuntimeError("NVFP4 tensor is missing rowwise data to replace")
91	    assert (
92	        old_rowwise.dtype == new_rowwise_data.dtype == torch.uint8
93	    ), "Rowwise NVFP4 storage must be uint8"
94	    # Preserve existing values and then swap storage
95	    new_rowwise_data.detach().copy_(old_rowwise)
96	    fp4_tensor._rowwise_data = new_rowwise_data
97	    del old_rowwise

100	def modify_grouped_nvfp4_rowwise_storage(
101	    grouped_tensor: torch.Tensor, new_rowwise_data: torch.Tensor
102	) -> None:
103	    """Replace grouped NVFP4 rowwise data with a new uint8 storage view.
104	
105	    The name intentionally mirrors `modify_nvfp4_rowwise_storage`: only the
106	    packed rowwise byte buffer is remapped into the DDP buffer. The grouped
107	    scale, amax, and columnwise buffers remain owned by the original tensor.
108	    """
109	    tensor = _unwrap_parameter_data(grouped_tensor)
110	    if not is_grouped_nvfp4tensor(tensor):
111	        raise ValueError("modify_grouped_nvfp4_rowwise_storage expects grouped NVFP4 storage")
112	
113	    old_rowwise = getattr(tensor, "rowwise_data", None)
114	    if old_rowwise is None:
115	        raise RuntimeError("Grouped NVFP4 tensor is missing rowwise data to replace")
116	
117	    new_rowwise_data = new_rowwise_data.view(-1)
118	    if old_rowwise.numel() != new_rowwise_data.numel():
119	        raise ValueError(
120	            "Grouped NVFP4 rowwise storage size mismatch: "
121	            f"old numel={old_rowwise.numel()}, new numel={new_rowwise_data.numel()}"
122	        )
123	    assert (
124	        old_rowwise.dtype == new_rowwise_data.dtype == torch.uint8
125	    ), "Grouped NVFP4 rowwise storage must be uint8"
126	
127	    new_rowwise_data.detach().copy_(old_rowwise.view(-1))

176	def get_fp4_align_size(fp4_recipe: Fp4Recipe) -> int:
177	    """
178	    Get the alignment size required for FP4 GEMM.
179	    FP4 GEMM requires Blackwell and later architectures.
180	
181	    The value 32 is a hardware requirement: TMA (Tensor Memory Accelerator) requires
182	    a 16-byte aligned address for efficient memory access. Since FP4 uses 4 bits per value,
183	    16 bytes (128 bits) corresponds to 32 FP4 values. Therefore, the alignment size for FP4
184	    is 32. With this alignment, NVFP4 GEMM can be performed efficiently.
185	
186	    Note that since we are also random hadamard transform for NVFP4 training, we want
187	    fused group nvfp4 quantize plus hadamard transform. Hadamard transform will leverage
188	    tensor core instructions for better performance, while group quantize kernels also
189	    prefer a more aligned size in token dimension M. The efficiently leverage grouped
190	    kernels, padding needs to be 64 multiple, but 128 multiple will bring even faster.
191	
192	    When it comes to MOE cuda graph support, the number of tokens for each expert should
193	    be a buffer on device memory, which means that we don't know the token dimension for
194	    each expertin host, therefore we cannot calculate the zero padded scaling factors shape
195	    on host to comply with the NVFP4 GEMM scaling factor layout. However, if we have already
196	    zero padded the tokens to 128 multiple, then there is no need for such padding, so that
197	    host doesn't need to copy the token distribution from device to host (which will break
198	    the CUDA graph).
199	
200	    Paper link: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.25149
201	    Scaling factor layout: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cublas/#d-block-scaling-factors-layout
202	    TE NVFP4 Grouped Quantization: https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/pull/2411
203	    """
204	    # pylint: disable=unused-argument
205	    return 128
